record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of almost periodic functions
record.original_question: Clarify the structural relationship between APr(R, C) and ℓ^r for 1<r<2. Since the paper states that APr appears to be modeled on ℓ^r because the Fourier series completely determines the generating function or equivalence class, determine in what precise sense APr is related to ℓ^r.

evidence.quote: Further, the fact that APr appears to be modeled on `r, because the Fourier series is completely determining the generating function/class, what more can be said about this relationship between APr and `r?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $1<r<2$. For a function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$, define the Marcinkiewicz–Besicovitch seminorm
$$\|f\|_{r}=\limsup_{T\to\infty}\Big(\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T}|f(t)|^{r}\,dt\Big)^{1/r},$$
and let $AP_{r}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C})$ denote the completion (modulo the kernel of $\|\cdot\|_{r}$) of the space of complex trigonometric polynomials $\sum_{k=1}^{N} a_k e^{i\lambda_k t}$ ($a_k\in\mathbb{C}$, $\lambda_k\in\mathbb{R}$) under this seminorm. For $f\in AP_r(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C})$, the Fourier–Bohr coefficients
$$c_\lambda(f)=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{2T}\int_{-T}^{T} f(t)e^{-i\lambda t}\,dt,\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb{R},$$
are nonzero only on a countable set, yielding a Fourier series $\sum_{n} c_n(f)\,e^{i\lambda_n t}$ that uniquely determines the equivalence class of $f$. Let $\ell^{r}$ denote the usual Banach space of $r$-summable complex sequences with norm $\|(a_n)\|_{\ell^r}=\big(\sum_n |a_n|^r\big)^{1/r}$.

Determine, in precise functional-analytic terms, the relationship between $AP_{r}(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C})$ and $\ell^{r}$. In particular, characterize for which $f\in AP_r(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C})$ the Fourier coefficient sequence lies in $\ell^r$, decide whether the Fourier coefficient map $f\mapsto (c_{\lambda_n}(f))_n$ embeds $AP_r(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C})$ continuously (or isomorphically) into $\ell^r$, and identify any natural Banach-space (e.g.\ isomorphism, isometric embedding, dense subspace, or duality) relationship between these two spaces.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns the structural relationship between the Marcinkiewicz–Besicovitch-type space $AP_r$ for $1<r<2$ and the sequence space $\ell^r$ via Fourier–Bohr coefficients. Standard references establish a Hausdorff–Young-type inclusion in the $B^2$ case (Parseval) and norm convergence of Fourier series for $1<q<\infty$ Besicovitch classes, but no precise Banach-space characterization (e.g. isomorphism or full Hausdorff–Young theorem) for $AP_r$ with $1<r<2$ appears in the surveyed literature. The problem appears open.

status_evidence.title: Fourier series of an almost-periodic function - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Besicovitch almost periodic functions in B2 have an expansion as a series with Σa_n^2 finite, and conversely every such series is the expansion of some Besicovitch periodic function.
status_evidence.claim: Only the case r=2 has a clean ℓ^2 (Parseval) characterization; the case 1<r<2 is not similarly characterized.

status_evidence.title: On convergence of Fourier series of Besicovitch almost periodic functions
status_evidence.snippet: Convergence in norm results for Fourier series of q-Besicovitch almost periodic functions for 1<q<∞.
status_evidence.claim: Fourier series convergence in $B^q$ norm is known, but does not give an $\ell^r$ identification.
